title: Minimum Cost Path with Alternating Directions II
summary: Given a grid with dimensions m by n, the cost to enter cell (i, j) is defined as (i + 1) * (j + 1).
statement: Given a grid with dimensions m by n, the cost to enter cell (i, j) is defined as (i + 1) * (j + 1). Additionally, a 2D array waitCost[i][j] defines the cost to wait in cell (i, j). The path starts at cell (0, 0) with an entrance cost. The movement follows an alternating pattern: on odd-numbered seconds, you must move right or down to an adjacent cell, paying its entry cost; on even-numbered seconds, you must wait in place for one second and pay the waitCost for that cell. The objective is to determine the minimum total cost required to reach cell (m - 1, n - 1).
constraints: Before each move except the first, pay one wait at the current cell.
hints: Every move after the first has one predecessor wait.
Add predecessor wait plus destination entry cost.
Every monotone route is represented by its final predecessor.
editorial: Every monotone route is represented by its final predecessor.
